title: WHO names responsive feeding as noticing hunger and fullness and answering them
summary: The infant-feeding sheet lists responsive feeding among its principles: recognize signs of hunger and fullness and respond.
body: Among the guiding principles for complementary feeding on the 4 August 2026 fact sheet, WHO includes responsive feeding. The sheet glosses that practice as recognizing and responding to signs of hunger and fullness. It is listed beside continued frequent breastfeeding, hygiene, and a gradual increase in amount, texture, and variety. The sheet names the practice. It does not print the gesture lists that the US CDC uses for babies and toddlers. Those gestures are separate cards. This is a recommendation about how feeding is offered, not a score of a child's appetite.

sources.title: Infant and young child feeding

sources.note: Paraphrase of the fact sheet. WHO text is not used under a CC BY licence, so this card does not quote it. Supports the responsive-feeding principle.
